planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil; space 3-4 feet apart for the mature mounded habit to fill in.

directions: This 2026 Proven Winners ColorChoice introduction is billed as the first diervilla with true jet-black foliage that holds its dark color from spring through frost rather than fading in summer heat. Small clusters of bright yellow, honeysuckle-like flowers appear against the near-black leaves in summer and draw bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds. The compact, mounded habit stays in the 3-4 foot range and tolerates heat, humidity, and dry spells once established, making it suited to mixed borders, rain gardens, and xeriscape plantings. It needs 4 or more hours of direct sun daily to develop and hold its darkest foliage color.

planting.note: Plant in full sun in average, well-drained garden soil; space 3-4 feet apart for a dense hedge or border effect.

directions: Introduced for 2026 as a faster-establishing successor to Sunjoy Neo, this barberry pushes out an especially robust root system early on, which the breeder says cuts down on watering needs during the first season. Small yellow flowers open in spring, but the main appeal is foliage: intensely saturated red leaves that hold their color from spring until frost, deeper than older Sunjoy selections. Its upright, rounded habit reaches roughly 3-5 feet tall and 3-4 feet wide, and it is noted as deer- and disease-resistant. Like other barberries it resents hard pruning, so any shaping should be light and done in late spring or early summer.

planting.note: Plant in moderately moist, well-drained soil in part to full sun; needs minimal pruning to maintain its naturally full form.

directions: New for 2026, this North American native arborvitae selection is distinguished by long, thread-like, fine-textured foliage that is noticeably denser than typical arborvitae, giving it a fuller, more elegant look in both garden beds and containers. The rich green, needle-like foliage provides year-round interest and needs very little pruning to stay full. Growing to roughly 3-5 feet tall and wide, it is promoted as a low-maintenance, evergreen alternative to boxwood for formal or informal hedges, borders, and decorative planters. It tolerates part sun but colors and fills in best with at least 4 hours of direct light daily.

common_name: Paraplu Pure White Rose of Sharon

planting.note: Plant in full sun in well-draining soil; blooms on new wood, so any pruning is best done in late winter or early spring.

directions: Part of the Paraplu rose-of-sharon line new for 2026, this selection is notable for flowers that open fully flat into perfectly round, pure-white blooms rather than the cupped or ruffled form typical of many hibiscus. The large flowers appear in heavy succession through summer since the plant blooms on new wood, and the pale color is said to glow especially brightly at dusk and dawn. It grows into an upright shrub around 5-8 feet tall and 5-6 feet wide, well suited to use as a specimen or informal flowering hedge. It needs a full 6 or more hours of direct sun daily and well-drained soil to perform at its best.

planting.note: Tolerates nearly any soil type as long as it drains; plant in full sun for the best silvery leaf color and heaviest berry set.

directions: New for 2026 and part of Proven Winners' Deer Proof collection, Silverstone cotoneaster is grown chiefly for its fuzzy, silvery-coated leaves, an unusual foliage color for the genus. Small white flowers open in spring and are followed by bright red berries that carry the plant through fall and into winter. Its low, wide, cascading habit tops out around 2-3 feet tall while spreading 4-6 feet, making it useful for edging, slopes, rock gardens, or groundcover-style plantings. It is drought-tolerant once established, resistant to fire blight, and reportedly rarely bothered by deer.

planting.note: Plant in moderately moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full to partial sun; allow room for its eventual 20-30 foot height when siting as a screen.

directions: Selected over a 40-year span from thousands of Thuja 'Nigra' seedlings and introduced for 2026, Sasquatch Dark Green is notable for being nearly seedless, which the breeder says channels the plant's energy into fuller, more vigorous growth instead of cone production. It forms a dense, uniformly conical, columnar evergreen with flat sprays of rich green foliage that deepens further in winter. Mature plants reach a substantial 20-30 feet tall but stay relatively narrow at 6-10 feet wide, making it suited to privacy screens and windbreaks rather than small gardens. It is noted for strong winter-burn resistance and tolerates both hot summers and severe cold once established.
